_comment: Raise a budget only in a pull request whose verification report explains why. See scripts/perf.ts.

budgets.reason: The core stylesheet ships to every consumer unconditionally; 0.7 adds a forced-colors block of about 0.3 KB, 0.9 adds the playground styles (about 0.9 KB gzip, measured).

Unminified source size of packages/doq/styles.css, the file consumers import. 0.9 adds about 6.3 KB for the playground (controls, toolbar, events, code panel, dialog, forced-colors and reduced-motion rules).

JavaScript loaded before a documentation page is interactive (entry + modulepreload chunks). Includes the host's Volt UI, Lumen Icons and Angular Movement; Doqs's own share is the part that grows with the library.

All JavaScript of the embedded showcase including lazy per-document chunks; grows with content, so a jump without new content is a regression. 0.10 adds two authored guides (current and archive) with source blocks and a playground; lazy per-document chunks only, initial JavaScript is unchanged within its budget.
Stylesheet linked by a documentation page (host styles + Doqs core).
Pagefind index, fragments and filters for the committed documents; scales with content and versions, not with library code. 0.10 adds two guides (current and the 1.x archive) to the index.

Pages prerendered for the committed content and its archive; an unexpected extra page means a duplicate route. 0.10 adds the generated Source-backed examples guide and its 1.x archive counterpart (21 + 2).

JavaScript loaded before a documentation page is interactive in the docs-first showcase (no host UI libraries). 0.11 raises the limit by 800 B: the measured growth from 0.10 is +959 B (194,019 to 194,978 B gzip) for landmark ownership in the three views, the unmatched route guard and the shell override; Showcase A grew by 815 B and the site by 32 B for the same code.
All JavaScript of the docs-first showcase including lazy per-document chunks. 0.10 adds three authored guides (two current, one archive); lazy per-document chunks only.
Stylesheet linked by a documentation page in the docs-first showcase. 0.9: the core stylesheet gained the playground styles (about 0.9 KB gzip).
Pagefind index, fragments and filters for the committed documents. 0.10 adds three guides (two current, one in the 1.x archive) to the index.
Pages prerendered for the committed content, its archive and the not-found view. 0.10 adds three generated guides (25 + 3).

JavaScript the official landing loads before it is interactive. It was 139,600 B before the site adopted Doqs for its own documentation; the documentation region (Doqs, Analog's Markdown renderer, Prism) is a lazy route, and an eager import of it measured 260,194 B.

All JavaScript of the official site including the lazy documentation chunks; grows with documentation content. 0.10 adds the Content authoring and Content tooling guides and 20 generated pages of the Content tooling API reference (the real reference of @doqs/analog/content, produced by doq-api from its declarations); lazy documentation chunks only, the landing's initial JavaScript is unchanged within its budget.

Stylesheet linked by the landing and the documentation (host Tailwind and Volt styles plus the Doqs core stylesheet). It was 11,160 B before the documentation was added. 0.9: the Doqs core stylesheet gained the playground styles (about 0.9 KB gzip).

Pagefind index of the official documentation (19 pages: 0.9 adds the Interactive playgrounds guide). 0.10 adds 22 documentation pages: two guides and the 20-page Content tooling API reference. 0.11 adds that one guide: measured 80,180 B, +5.7 KB over the 0.10 figure (74,5xx B).

The landing, the documentation index and 19 documents (0.9 adds the Interactive playgrounds guide); an unexpected extra page means a duplicate route. The landing, the documentation index and 41 documents: 0.10 adds two guides and the 20-page Content tooling API reference (21 + 22). 0.11 adds the guide Adopting Doqs in an existing library site (44 pages).

Analog bundles the frontmatter and a loader of every Markdown file of every version into the first-loaded JavaScript; Doqs cannot lazy-load that through a supported Analog API. Measured 20 -> 200 generated documents (+ half as many archived): 52 B gzip per document; 20 -> 1000: 46 B. A jump means Doqs added per-document work to the browser bundle.
